abstract: <jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title><jats:p>Septoria tritici blotch (STB), caused by <jats:italic>Mycosphaerella graminicola</jats:italic> (synonym: <jats:italic>Zymoseptoria tritici</jats:italic>; asexual stage: <jats:italic>Septoria tritici</jats:italic>), is an important disease of wheat (<jats:italic>Triticum aestivum</jats:italic> L.) worldwide. Management of the disease usually is by host resistance or fungicides. However, <jats:italic>M. graminicola</jats:italic> has developed insensitivity to most commonly applied fungicides, so there is a continuing need for well‐characterized sources of host resistance to accelerate the development of improved wheat cultivars. Gene <jats:italic>Stb3</jats:italic> has been a useful source of major resistance, but its mapping location has not been well characterized. On the basis of linkage to a single marker, a previous study assigned <jats:italic>Stb3</jats:italic> to a location on the short arm of chromosome 6D. However, the results from the present study show that this reported location is incorrect. Instead, linkage analysis revealed that <jats:italic>Stb3</jats:italic> is located on the short arm of wheat chromosome 7A, completely linked to microsatellite (simple‐sequence repeat) locus <jats:italic>Xwmc83</jats:italic> and flanked by loci <jats:italic>Xcfa2028</jats:italic> (12.4 cM distal) and <jats:italic>Xbarc222</jats:italic> (2.1 cM proximal). Linkage between <jats:italic>Stb3</jats:italic> and <jats:italic>Xwmc83</jats:italic> was validated in BC<jats:sub>1</jats:sub>F<jats:sub>3</jats:sub> progeny of other crosses, and analyses of the flanking markers with deletion stocks showed that the gene is located on 7AS between fraction lengths 0.73 and 0.83. This revised location of <jats:italic>Stb3</jats:italic> is different from those for other STB resistance genes previously mapped in hexaploid wheat but is approximately 20 cM proximal to an STB resistance gene mapped on the short arm of chromosome 7A<jats:sup>m</jats:sup> in <jats:italic>Triticum monococcum</jats:italic>. The markers described in this study are useful for accelerating the deployment of <jats:italic>Stb3</jats:italic> in wheat breeding programs.</jats:p>
title: A New Map Location of Gene Stb3 for Resistance to Septoria Tritici Blotch in Wheat
